ῥάδιξ.definition: branch, Nic.Th.378,533, Al.57,331; of the palm, frond, D.S.2.53

ῥαφίς.definition: garfish, Belone acus, Epich.l.c., Arist.Fr.294, Opp.H.1.172, C.2.392

ῥάφυς.definition: = Speus. ap. Ath.9.369b; perh. to be read in Numen.ib.371c; cf

ῥέανσις.definition: prob. = polishing with wine as a cleanser , Stud.Pal.22.183.109

ῥέγμα.definition: ) that which is dyed, Ibyc.10 B; cf

ῥείτης.definition: only in Gramm., as part of the compds. Choerob.inAn.Ox.2.256, etc

ῥέος.definition: like anything flowing, stream, A.Ag.901, Pr.676, 812; also of tears, ib.401

ῥῆμα.definition: that which is said or spoken; phrase, opp. , Pl.Cra.399b, Aeschin.3.72; Pl.Lg.840c

ῥήν.definition: sheep, lamb , A.R.4.1497; Nic.Th.453. ; [i.e. perh. Id.)

ῥήτωρ.definition: one who gives sentence, judge, S.Fr.1090; advocate, POxy.37.4 , etc

ῥίζις.definition: an Ethiopian animal of the elephant kind, Str.17.3.5

ῥίσκος.definition: coffer, chest, esp. for plate or money; sarcophagus, IG14.1934f3

ῥῖψις.definition: throwing, hurling; being thrown or hurled, Pl.R.378d; Plu.Lys.12; throwing oneself, Id.2.166a

ῥοάς.definition: shedding of fruit, a disease of vines, f.l. for Thphr.HP4.14.6

ῥογίον.definition: receiver of a still, Zos.Alch.p.142 B

ῥόδον.definition: metaplast. dat. pl. v.l. in; = Rev.Hist.Rel.97.275

ῥόθος.definition: rushing noise, roar of waves, dash of oars; of any confused, inarticulate sound, the noise of the Persian tongue, ib.406; but there is tumult or confusion, when Justice is dragged whithersoever bribed judges lead her,…

ῥοῖβδος.definition: any rushing noise or motion, whirring of wings, S.Ant.1004; rushing of the wind, Ar.Nu.407

ῥοΐδιον.definition: Dim. of small pomegranate; rind of pomegranate, Gloss

ῥοΐσκος.definition: Dim. of small pomegranate: hence, knob or tassel shaped like a pomegranate, LXXEx.28.29, al., J.AJ3.7.4

ῥόμβος.definition: or bull-roarer, instrument; magic wheel, spun alternately in each direction by the torsion of two cords passed through two holes in it, used as a love-charm, Luc.DMeretr.4.5; called in Theoc.2.17, AP5.204; Lat. rhombu…

ῥομφαία.definition: large, broad sword, used by the Thracians

ῥόπαλον.definition: club, cudgel, used to beat an ass; membrum virile, APl.4.261

ῥοῦς.definition: Att. contr. for; and uncontr. acc. sg. masc

ῥυάς.definition: fluid, flaccid, flabby; falling off, hair that is shed, Id.Pr.898a32; a vine that sheds its grapes, Thphr.HP4.14.6 , Gp.5.39.1

ῥύμα.definition: = anything that flows, stream, IG9 .692.5 : metaph., Orph.H.10.22; Procl.H.1.4

ῥῦμα.definition: ) that which is drawn; i.e. the Persian archers, opp. i.e. the Greek spearmen, A.Pers.147 ; from the distance of a bow-shot, X.An.3.3.15; Eun.Hist.p.271D

ῥύπος.definition: dirt, filth, used by Hom. once in; metaph., sordidness, meanness, M.Ant.7.47

ῥύτις.definition: = in a play on words, Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch.p.119 B

ῥύτρος.definition: a plant with prickles at the ends, globe-thistle, Echinops viscosus, Thphr.HP6.4.4

ῥύτωρ.definition: ) one who draws, of Apollo, Ar.Th.108; ) saviour, deliverer

ῥωβίδας.definition: at Sparta, boy of less than one year old, in SteinHerodotus ii p.465

ῥώμη.definition: bodily strength, might, Xenoph.2.11; of nations, armies, and the like , Th.4.18

ῥώξ.definition: breach: in Od.22.143, the sense is dub.; it seems to mean narrow entrances or passages leading to the hall

ῥῶσταξ.definition: stand for putting anything on, Tz.H.11.612

ῥαβδίον.definition: Dim. of little rod or shoot; divining-rod, LXXEz.21.21

ῥαβδοῦχος.definition: one who carries a rod or; judge, umpire at a contest, Pl.Prt.338a

ῥάβδωσις.definition: fluting of columns, etc; = virgultum, dub. in Gloss

ῥάζω.definition: = , snarl, as a dog, metaph. of men, Cratin.25

ῥαίνω.definition: Pi.I.8.50, Xenarch.7.7: fut; sprinkle, besprinkle, with acc. of the object besprinkled

ῥαίω.definition: poet. subj. Od.5.221: fut; generally, destroy, A.R.1.617:—Pass., to be broken down, crushed by suffering, . . A.Pr.191, AP7.529 , etc. , cf. S.Tr.268

ῥάκινος.definition: ragged, Michel 832.17, al; a substance used in alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.185 B

ῥακόω.definition: in Pass., become ragged or wrinkled, of skins; in Pass., to be dispersed all about, . . Hp.Morb.4.49

ῥακτήριος.definition: fit for striking with; broken, discordant , Id.Fr.699

ῥάκωσις.definition: a becoming ragged or wrinkled, of the skin, when the flesh under it is shrunk, Sor.2.40, Zen.6.42

ῥάμφος.definition: crooked beak of birds of prey: generally, beak, bill, Ar.Av.99, Pl.Com.138, Plu.2.980e; cf

ῥανίς.definition: semen virile, AP10.45; metaph., drop, spot, Ael.NA17.23, cf. 38; Philostr.VA3.48

ῥαντήρ.definition: one who wets, esp. of the; sprinkler, Mon.Ant.23.150

ῥάπτω.definition: Od.16.422, etc.: fut. Aeschin.2.21; metaph. c. dat., devise, contrive, plot, Od.3.118, cf. Il.18.367; Od.16.379,422; E.IT681; also Hdt.9.17; E.Andr.911; Lat. suere dolos, Alex.98.2: prov., you sewed the shoe but A. pu…

ῥᾳστώνη.definition: Ion. easiness of doing; easiness of temper, good nature, mildness, c. gen. objecti, from kindness to Democedes, Hdt.3.136; Plb.38.11.11

ῥαφεύς.definition: stitcher, patcher, cobbler; metaph., planner of murder, A.Ag.1604

ῥαχόω.definition: cover with wattle-work, prob. in IG22.463.82

ῥέγκος.definition: snoring, stertorous breathing, Hp.Acut.17, Epid.5.55; also Erot. s.v. and Hp.Epid.5.104, 7.77; cf. sq

ῥέζω.definition: freq. in Ep. and Trag. , but rare; do, act, deal, opp. Od.4.205, 22.314; opp. v. infr.:—Constr

ῥεκτήρ.definition: worker, doer, like Homer's; c. gen. objecti, worker in a thing, Man.1.297, cf. 4.149

ῥεμβασμός.definition: roaming about: metaph., wavering, anxious turn of mind, ib.Wi.4.12

ῥέπω.definition: mostly used in pres. and impf.: fut; more generally, of things, incline one way or the other, what is always shifling, never steady, Pi.O.8.23; inclines downward, falls, of a young girl's eye, A.Fr.242; sleep falling …

ῥέω.definition: Il.22.149, etc.; Ep. Hes.Fr.263 , D.P.1074, AP7.36 , but not in Hom.: impf. 3sg. Il.17.86, Telecl.1.4, but elsewhere in Hom. or fut. Thgn.448, E.Fr.384, Crates Com.15.4, Pherecr.130.5, Hp.Haem.5; also Arist.Mete.356a1…

ῥῆγμα.definition: breakage, fracture, joined; laceration, rupture, Gal.10.160, 18.882, cf. Arist.HA635a4

ῥήγνυμι.definition: or Hp.Flat.10: impf; break a line of battle or body of men, Il.6.6, 11.538, 15.615; break through the centre, Hdt.6.113: abs., . . broke through, S.Fr.210.9:— Med., break oneself a way through the lines, Il.11.90, 13.…

ῥήκτης.definition: breaker, render; of an earthquake that breaks the earth into fissures, Arist.Mu.396a5, Lyd.Ost.54

ῥηξίνοος.definition: breaking the wits, of Dionysus, ib.524.18

ῥητινόω.definition: flavour with resin, Dsc.Eup.2.65: pf. part. Pass. mixed with resin, Hp.Art.62

ῥητορεύω.definition: to be a public speaker, practise oratory; teach oratory, Str.14.1.48

ῥητότης.definition: rationality, of numbers, Iamb.in Nic.p.91 P

ῥήτρα.definition: Ion. Elean v. infr; in the Doric and Elean dialects, compact, treaty, SIG9

ῥιγέω.definition: cool or slacken in zeal, Pi.N.5.50; bristle with arms, . . Theoc.l.c

ῥιγόλυτον.definition: hot bath administered to an epileptic patient, cj. in Cael.Aur.TP1.93

ῥιγόω.definition: fut. X.Mem.2.1.17, Ep. inf. Od.14.481: aor. Ar.Pl.846: pf. Thphr.Ign.74 , Gal.11.556.—Like has an irreg. contr. into for 3sg. subj. Pl.Grg.517d, cj. in Phd.85a; opt. Hp.Int.10, Plu.2.233a; inf. Ar.Ach.1146, V.446, Av.…

ῥιζάγρα.definition: instrument for extracting the roots of a tooth, Cels.7.12.1, Paul.Aeg.6.88

ῥιζίας.definition: made from the root of a plant, opp. Thphr.HP6.3.2, 9.1.7, cf. Plin.HN19.43

ῥιζοτόμος.definition: one who cuts or gathers roots; as Adj., the time for cutting roots, Nic.Th.494

ῥιζοφυής.definition: putting out roots, ib.1.8.1; growing from a root, Id.HP7.10.1

ῥιζόω.definition: cause to strike root: metaph., plant, fix; metaph., Hdt.1.64:—Pass., ib.60, cf. Pl.Lg.839a; have their root in . . , Id.Ep.336b, cf. S.E.Med.1.271; Ep.Eph.3.18

ῥίζωμα.definition: the mass of roots of a tree; element, Emp.6.1; Pythag.15

ῥιναυλέω.definition: blow through the nose, snort, from anger, cj. for in Luc.Lex.19

ῥινάω.definition: lead by the nose, Pherecr.23, Men.895:—Pass., we were chaffed, Alciphr.Fr.6.2

ῥίνημα.definition: that which is filed; an eyesalve, Gal.12.778

ῥινολαβίς.definition: instrument for taking hold of the nose, Id

ῥινοτόμος.definition: piercing shields or hides, dub.l. for in Nonn.D.21.87

ῥιπή.definition: poet. Noun, swing or force with; flapping of wings, A.Pr.126 , cf. E.Fr.594.4; buzz of a gnat's wing, A.Ag.893; of the lyre's quivering notes, Pi.P.1.10

ῥιπίς.definition: fan for raising the fire; lady's fan, Stratt.56, AP6.290 , D.H.7.9

ῥιπτάζω.definition: Frequentat. of throw to and fro, toss; Pass. also, = AP5.164

ῥίπτω.definition: like toss oneself about, as in a fever, Hp.Mul.1.2; AP5.118 : generally, throw about, E.IA758, cf. Ba.150 ; winnow, Gal.6.541

ῥιψαύχην.definition: tossing the neck , properly of horses: metaph., Pi.Dith.Oxy.1604 ii 13

ῥίψοπλος.definition: throwing away one's arms, of a panic flight, A.Th.315

ῥοδῆ.definition: contr. for = rose-bush, Archil.29, Asclep.Myrl. ap. Ath.2.50e, Pamphil. ib.52f; Ion. A.R.3.1020

ῥοδίζω.definition: to be like the rose, Ath.15.677e; trans., scent with roses, Thphr.Od.47; Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.12

ῥοδίς.definition: pastille made from roses, Dsc.1.99.3, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.133

ῥοδόμηλον.definition: Dor. rose-apple: metaph; a confection of roses and quinces, Alex.Trall.1.10

ῥοθέω.definition: make a rushing noise: hence, of a; of any confused noise, . . such clamours they raised against me, S.Ant.290; . . there was a noise of angry words, ib.259

ῥοθιάζω.definition: strengthd. form of foreg., ply the dashing; of pigs eating, make a guttling noise, Id.Ach.807; cf. I.2

ῥοιβδέω.definition: move with a whistling or rustling sound; suck down, of Charybdis, Od.12.106; Ezek.Exag.237, cf. Aristid.Or.46.38

ῥοιζέω.definition: Ion. and Ep. impf. Hes.Th.835: aor. Opp. , Ep. Il.10.502:—Pass., v. infr.: :—whistle, Il.l.c.; of a snake, hiss, Hes. l.c., A.R.4.129, etc.; Opp.H.1.563; of birds, rush or whirr through the air, Luc.Am.22, cf. Arist.H…

ῥοιζήτωρ.definition: one who moves with a rushing sound, Orph.H.6.5,8.6

ῥοῖζος.definition: Ion. whistling or whizzing of an arrow; rushing motion, rush, swing, Plu.Marc.15, Demetr.21, Epic. in Arch.Pap. 7 p.4

ῥομβόω.definition: bring into the shape of a rhombus, HeroBel.102.12

ῥοπή.definition: turn of the scale, fall of the scale-; metaph., balancing, suspense, Alc.25; A.Ch.61 ; S.Tr.82; . . staking distant ventures on nice balancings, Id.Fr.555 ; the turning- point or sinking-point of life, i.e. death, Id.…

ῥοφέω.definition: drain dry, empty, Ar.Ach.278, Eq.905; so of the poison on the robe of Heracles, S.Tr.1055

ῥοχθέω.definition: dash with a roaring sound, of the sea, Od.5.402; 12.60; sounded with the dashing of the waves, A.R.4.925; Opp.H.1.228.—Cf
